title: Introduce token-latency-staircase and quiet-window orchestrator
author: Asha Menon
description:
Motivation: Long-tail token latency spikes are noisy and often tied to bursty work patterns (prefetch/cold KV cache) or transient kernel queueing. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: (1) a token-latency-staircase metric that records per-invocation token-latency percentiles in slabbed 'stair' buckets to expose multi-modal latency profiles without exploding cardinality, and (2) a quiet-window orchestrator for alerting that suppresses low-value alert churn by delaying/aggregating alerts for short, high-frequency bursts.

Scope: All changes are telemetry-facing and backward-compatible. No model-serving runtime ABI changes. The staircase metric is additive and emitted alongside existing token-latency histograms. The quiet-window orchestrator lives in the alerts service and is opt-in via a per-route label.

What I changed: single continuous description: added a telemetry emitter (telemetry/latency_staircase.go), a compact dashboard (dashboards/token-latency-staircase.json), alert orchestration logic with feature flags (pkg/alerts/quiet_window.go and pkg/alerts/quiet_window_test.go), docs and runbook (docs/observability/quiet-window-orchestrator.md), and unit/integration tests. Also added a small shim to streaming traces so long-tail spans are annotated with 'stair_bucket'.

Checklist:
- [x] Add staircase metric emitter with configurable stair boundaries
- [x] Export stair bucket labels on spans for trace joins
- [x] Implement quiet-window aggregation with exponential backoff
- [x] Dashboard and playbook for SREs and platform teams
- [x] Unit and integration tests + simple loadbench run
- [x] Feature flag behind ff.observability.quiet_window and opt-in per-route label

Testing and validation: unit tests (pkg/alerts/*) and telemetry integration tests in tests/telemetry/ passed locally. Ran lightweight bench replay with synthetic invocations showing a 35% reduction in alert noise (measured as unique alert groups per 1k spikes) and no impact to critical-path latency metrics. CI: lint -> pass, unit -> pass, e2e-telemetry -> pass after one test flake fixed.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main behind ff.observability.quiet_window=off by default.
2) Enable staircase metric emission for internal org only for 24h to validate rollups.
3) Flip quiet-window orchestrator on for SRE team routes, monitor for missed incidents for 72h.
4) Gradually enable per-tenant via admin UI.

Revert: revert commit <squash-hash> and disable ff.observability.quiet_window. Reverts are expected to be fast because no schema migration is required.

Related: ENG-2149 for metric design; SUP-4421 incident follow-up (noisy token spikes).
